draft.title: What makes a business succeed
card: No single thing makes a business succeed. Successful businesses usually do several things well at the same time.
Real need
the business sells something people want and will pay for. Planning means thinking ahead about customers, costs and goals.
Money and customers
the business keeps track of what it earns and spends, so it does not run out of money. It also treats customers well, so they come back.
Adapting
when things change, such as new rivals or new tastes, the business changes too. Businesses that ignore change can lose customers.
draft.remember: Successful businesses usually meet a need, plan, manage money, look after customers and adapt.

a.q: Which is the best reason a new business is likely to succeed?
opts: It sells something many people want and will pay for
It has a bright logo and a catchy name
It opened in a spot where there are no other shops
It was started by a person who has lots of friends
a.why: A business that meets a real need has customers who will pay, which it must have to keep going. A catchy name may get attention, but it does not give people a reason to keep buying.
a.clue: Think about why people would hand over money.

b.q: Jas runs a bike repair stall in Hobart. Many customers now ride e-bikes, which he cannot fix. He learns how to repair them and keeps his stall busy. Which idea does this show?
opts: Adapting when things change
Managing money carefully
Meeting a need that no one else meets
Keeping customers happy with low prices
b.why: Jas changed what he does because his customers' bikes changed. That is adapting. Keeping customers happy is related, but the card's step here is about responding to a change, not about prices.
b.clue: What changed, and what did Jas do about it?

a.best: It sells something many people want and will pay for

problems.detail: Why (a) says meeting a need is something the business 'must' have to keep going. The card says successful businesses 'usually' do these things, so 'must' overstates it.

check.summary: The card and both questions are sound, and each question has one clear answer. The only problem is that why (a) uses 'must' where the card says 'usually'.
